BURSEVI:v10p314/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p314/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p314/r10.claim: When pasture dries, it turns black whether heat or cold caused the withering; the quick sequence hints at the world's short life and fading pleasure.
BURSEVI:v10p314/r10.anchor: أسود من الحوة بمعنى السواد وذلك أن الكلأ إذا جف ويبس أسود سواء كان جفافه

QASHANI:87:5/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:87:5/r1.claim: Worldly pasture quickly perishes like blackened brittle stubble; do not turn toward or occupy yourself with it, lest it block special glorification and conceal your destined perfection, which alone endures.
QASHANI:87:5/r1.anchor: سريع الفناء وشيك الزوال كالهشيم والحطام البالي المسود فلا تلتفت إليه ولا تشتغل به

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the plants became dry, crumbled matter and turned discolored.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : فجعله غثاء قال : هشيما احوى قال : متغيرا

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r2.claim: Mujahid glosses the debris as flood detritus and ahwa as black.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3416#3/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد فجعله غثاء احوى قال : غثاء السيل . و احوى قال : اسود

IBNASHUR:87:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried vegetation; it may be pronounced with a light or doubled thāʾ.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r1.anchor: والغثاء : بضم الغين المعجمة وتخفيف المثلثة ، ويقال بتشديد المثلثة هو اليابس من النبت

IBNASHUR:87:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r2.claim: Aḥwā describes a brown approaching black; dry plants turn this color as their green fades.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r2.anchor: الموصوف بالحُوَّة بضم الحاء وتشديد الواو

IBNASHUR:87:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r3.claim: The color change from fresh green to dark dry growth evokes God's power to bring things into being and end them.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r3.anchor: لاستحضار تغيُّر لونه بعد أن كان أخضر يانعاً وذلك دليل على تصرفه تعالى بالإنشاء وبالإنهاء

IBNASHUR:87:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r4.claim: The pasture stands for Qur'anic guidance and law as rain-grown pasture benefits animals; the law likewise reaches its completion and full maturity.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r4.anchor: إيماء إلى تمثيل حال القرآن وهدايته وما اشتمل عليه من الشريعة التي تنفع الناس بحال الغيث

IBNASHUR:87:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR:87:5/r5.claim: A prophetic report compares the guidance and knowledge brought by the Prophet to abundant rain: receptive land grows abundant pasture, while land that retains water benefits people in other ways.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r5.anchor: بقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم « مثل ما بَعَثني الله به من الهُدى والعِلم

IBNASHUR:87:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r6.claim: The verse may also teach that created things pass through opposite stages, recalling death after life and the brevity of worldly freshness.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r6.anchor: إدماج العبرة بتصاريف ما أودع الله في المخلوقات من مختلف الأطوار من الشيء إلى ضده للتذكير بالفناء بعد الحياة

IBNASHUR:87:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:87:5/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:87:5/r7.claim: The quick sequence marked by the particle in “then He made it dry” underscores how briefly the world's flourishing lasts, as in the parable of the harvested crop.
IBNASHUR:87:5/r7.anchor: الحرفُ الموضوع لعطف ما يحصل فيه حكم المعطوف بعدَ زمن قريب من زمن حصول المعطوف عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r1.claim: After the grass is green, God makes it ghuthāʾ: dries it into brittle matter like the scum floating on floodwater; this was also discussed at 23:41.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r1.anchor: فجعله بعد الخضرة غثاء قال الزجاج أي جففه حتى جعله هشيما جافا كالغثاء الذي تراه فوق ماء السيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says aḥwā means blackened by age, or that the grass emerges blackish against its green; compare the two dark-green gardens in 55:64.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p89#2/r2.anchor: فأما قوله تعالى أحوى فقال الفراء الأحوى الذي قد اسود عن القدم والعتق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r6.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r6.claim: They explain the pasture becoming dark as withered, discolored plant matter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هشيما متغيرا. وعن مجاهد، وقتادة، وابن زيد، نحوه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r7.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r7.claim: A grammarian proposed reversed word order: God brought forth dark-green pasture, then made it dry litter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r7.anchor: قال ابن جرير: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب (4) يرى أن ذلك من المؤخر الذي معناه التقديم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r8.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r8.claim: Ibn Jarir calls the reversed-order reading possible but wrong because it conflicts with the exegetes' transmitted explanations.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p379/r8.anchor: ثم قال ابن جرير: وهذا وإن كان محتملا إلا أنه غير صواب؛ لمخالفته أقوال أهل التأويل.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r1.anchor:
{فجعله غثاء} أي يبسا.
{أحوى} أسود من قدمه واحتراقه (2)

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r2.claim: Aḥwā means blackened by age and burning.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p524#2/r2.anchor:
{فجعله غثاء} أي يبسا.
{أحوى} أسود من قدمه واحتراقه (2)

KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:3/r4.claim: A lighter reading has qaddara; ahwa is an adjective of ghutha, meaning the pasture that He brought forth.

KASHSHAF:87:5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:5/r1.claim: After its greenness and freshness, the pasture becomes dark debris.

KASHSHAF:87:5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:87:5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:87:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, ahwa describes the pasture when first brought forth, dark from intense greenness and moisture, before it becomes debris.
KASHSHAF:87:5/r2.anchor: أخرجه أحوى أسود من شدّة الخضرة والري

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p739/r9.claim: Ahwa can qualify the dried herbage: God grows pasture, then makes it dark withered chaff after its greenness; alternatively it describes the pasture as dark green before it becomes chaff.

MAJAZ:v2p295/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p295/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p295/r1.claim: Aḥwā can mean blackened by burning into brittle plant remains; elsewhere it describes intensely green, well-watered growth.
MAJAZ:v2p295/r1.anchor: هيجه حتى ليس فجعله أسود من احتراقه غثاء هشيما وهو فى موضع آخر من شدة خضرته وكثرة مائه

MAJAZ:v2p295/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p295/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p295/r2.claim: Dhu al-Rumma’s verse uses ḥawwāʾ for lush green growth, illustrating the other sense of aḥwā.
MAJAZ:v2p295/r2.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: قرحاء حواء أشراطية وكفت ... فيها الذهاب وحفتها البراعيم

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r3.claim: Ghutha is dried, brittle vegetation scattered by the wind, and ahwa means black; Dhu al-Rumma's verse supports the color sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r3.anchor: وهذا معنى قول مجاهد . الثاني : أن الغثاء ما

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r4.speaker: ذي الرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r4.claim: His verse uses ḥawa for dark coloring of lips and related features.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r5.claim: He says ghutha is plants carried by a flood and ahwa means changed in color.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r6.claim: A third reading uses reversed order: ahwa describes the living plant's colors before it becomes ghutha; all those colors may be called black, as in Sawad Iraq.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r6.anchor: ومعناه أحوى فصار غثاء , والأحوى : ألوان النبات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r7.speaker: امرؤ القيس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r7.claim: His line is cited as evidence for the term ahwa describing dark vegetation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p252/r7.anchor: وقال امرؤ القيس : وغيث دائم التهتا

MUJAHID:v2p751#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p751#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p751#3/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses ghutha as flood debris and ahwa as dry.
MUJAHID:v2p751#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد قال الغثاء ﴿ غثاء ﴾ السيل و الأحوى اليابس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p332#5/r1.claim: God made the pasture dry and brittle refuse; ahwa means black and grammatically qualifies the refuse.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r1.claim: Guthāʾ is debris—grass, plants, and rubbish—cast along a valley by flood; it can also mean dry, broken vegetation or foam and refuse floating on water.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r1.anchor: الغثاء: ما يقذف به السيل على جوانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات والقماش.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r2.claim: Qatada says guthāʾ means something dried out; it is also said of crushed, dried greens and refuse around water.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r2.anchor: قتادة: الغثاء: الشيء اليابس. ويقال للبقل والحشيش إذا تحطم ويبس: غثاء وهشيم.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r3.claim: Aḥwā means black; intense greenness turns toward black. The term can describe dark lips, and an aḥwā camel has green mixed with black and yellow.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r3.anchor: والأحوى: الأسود أي أن النبات يضرب إلى الحوة من شدة الخضرة كالأسود.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r4.claim: Grammatically aḥwā may be a circumstantial modifier of pasture, describing its dark green state before it becomes debris, or an adjective of the debris after drying.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r4.anchor: ثم قيل: يجوز أن يكون «أحوى» حالا من «المرعى»، ويكون المعنى: كأنه من خضرته يضرب إلى السواد

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r5.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says the vegetation turns black after drying and burning; a plant in its fresh state later darkens.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: فجعله أسود من احتراقه وقدمه والرطب إذا يبس اسود.

QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r6.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says God first brings it out green, then it dries, blackens, and is carried away by wind and flood, exemplifying worldly beauty’s passing.
QURTUBI-FULL:87:5/r6.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: أخرج المرعى أخضر، ثم لما يبس اسود من احتراقه

NAHHAS:v5p203/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r19.claim: One parse makes aḥwā describe the extracted pasture as dark-green before God made it dry growth.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r19.anchor: أحدهما والذي أخرج المرعى أحوى أي أخضر يضرب إلى السواد فجعله غثاء

NAHHAS:v5p203/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r20.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p203/r20.claim: The better parse makes the pasture turn into dark, dry debris; forced inversion is warranted only when the ordinary sense fails.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r20.anchor: والقول الآخر والذي أخرج المرعى فجعله غثاء أسود وهذا أولى بالصواب وإنما يقع التقديم والتأخير

NAHHAS:v5p203/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p203/r21.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p203/r21.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the result as dry, changed plant matter.
NAHHAS:v5p203/r21.anchor: وقد روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس فجعله غثاء أحوى يقول هشيما متغيرا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r1.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r3.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:1/r4.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r1.claim: Vegetation begins green then withers into dark, almost black debris; it can feed creatures in either state, each suited to some purpose in life by God's measure.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r1.anchor: والمرعى يخرج في أول أمره خضرا

QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r2.claim: The plant's withering quietly suggests that every growth is harvested and every living thing ends, linking worldly life to the enduring afterlife.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r2.anchor: والإشارة إلى حياة النبات هنا توحي من طرف خفي

QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r3.claim: The broad cosmic frame connects the surah's subsequent truths to existence, and similarly frames many surahs in this section in harmony with their mood and rhythm.
QUTB-ZILAL:87:5/r3.anchor: وبهذا المطلع الذي يكشف عن هذا المدى المتطاول من صفحة الوجود الكبيرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r1.claim: Ghutha is dried vegetation carried away by valleys, floodwaters, and winds; Qutrub gives ghutha'a as its singular form.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r1.anchor: الغثاء ما يبس من النبت فحملته الأودية والمياه

RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r2.claim: One view says ahwa means blackness or a color tending to black when wet; as an adjective for debris, it describes pasture turning dark after it dries.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r2.anchor: الحوة السواد ، وقال بعضهم : الأحوى هو الذي يضرب إلى السواد

RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r3.claim: This darkening may result from cold drying the grass, mud deposited by floods, or dust attached by wind.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r3.anchor: وسبب ذلك السواد أمور أحدها : أن العشب إنما يجف

RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r4.claim: Al-Farra and Abu Ubayda instead take ahwa as black through intense greenness, like the description mudhammtan.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r4.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو اختيار الفراء وأبي عبيدة ، وهو أن يكون الأحوى هو الأسود

RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r5.claim: On that alternative syntax, God brought forth dark-green pasture and then made it debris, like a verse describing a revelation as upright while denying that it is crooked.
RAZI-FULL:v31p127#2/r5.anchor: والتقدير الذي أخرج المرعى أحوى فجعله غثاء

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ can be a second object or circumstantial, and both geminated and light thāʾ are used; it means vegetation deposited by a flood along a valley.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r1.anchor: إما مفعول ثان، وإما حال. والغثاء بتشديد الثاء وتخفيفها

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r2.speaker: امرؤ القيس
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r2.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays compares the hilltop to a spindle whorl among flood debris, attesting ghuthāʾ for flood-borne plant matter.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r2.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: 4549 كأن ذرا رأس المجيمر غدوة من السيل والغثاء

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ transmits a plural form al-agthāʾ, unusual because it pluralizes a faʿāl noun on afʿāl.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r3.anchor: ورواه الفراء " والأغثاء " على الجمع. وفيه غرابة

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r4.claim: Aḥwā most clearly modifies ghuthāʾ, though it can be a circumstantial from al-marʿā; the author rejects Abū al-Baqāʾ's label of fronting part of a relative clause.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r4.anchor: فيه وجهان، أظهرهما: أنه نعت ل " غثاء ". والثاني: أنه حال من " المرعى ".

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r5.claim: Aḥwā derives from ḥawa, dark coloring tending toward green; another explanation is green with a dark overlay, or a dark-backed gazelle, and the word inflects as shown.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r5.anchor: والأحوى: أفعل من الحوة وهي سواد يضرب إلى الخضرة.

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r6.speaker: ذو الرمة
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r6.claim: Dhū al-Rumma's line uses ḥawa for dark coloring on a woman's lips, an instance previously invoked in the debate over mistaken apposition.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r6.anchor: قال ذو الرمة: 4550 لمياء في شفتيها حوة لعس

SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r7.claim: The cited line calls a fawn aḥwā and mentions its paired markings along the back.
SAMIN-DURR:87:5/r7.anchor: قال: 4551 وفي الحي أحوى ينفض المرد شادن

STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.claim: The pasture and its blackened stubble illustrate God’s power over the creation and destruction of living things; marʿā means all forms of vegetation.
STUDYQURAN:87:4/r1.anchor: These verses allude to the manner in which God maintains power over the creation and destruction of all living things

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the debris as brittle and discolored.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: " {غثاء أحوى} [الأعلى: 5] يقول: هشيما متغيرا "

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r2.claim: Mujāhid compares it to dark flood debris and glosses ahwā as black.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: " {غثاء أحوى} [الأعلى: 5] قال: غثاء السيل أحوى، قال: أسود "

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says the vegetation returns to dryness after being green.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله : " {غثاء أحوى} [الأعلى: 5] قال: يعود يبسا بعد خضرة "

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd describes green plants drying into dark debris that wind and floods carry away.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: " {فجعله غثاء أحوى} [سورة: الأعلى، آية رقم: 5] قال: كان بقلا ونباتا أخضر، ثم هاج فيبس

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r5.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r5.claim: Some Arabists reorder the sense: God first brings out dark-green pasture, then makes it debris, citing Dhū al-Rumma’s description of dark-green vegetation.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r5.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب يرى أن ذلك من المؤخر الذي معناه التقديم

TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r6.claim: Ṭabarī rejects reordering because Arabs may call intensely green plants black, and inversion is unnecessary when the words make good sense in their present order.
TAB-FULL:v24p313#2/r6.anchor: وهذا القول وإن كان غير مدفوع أن يكون ما اشتدت خضرته من النبات، قد تسميه العرب أسود، غير صواب عندي

TABATABAI:87:17-19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r8.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r8.claim: Uqba ibn ʿĀmir reports that the Prophet instructed worshippers to place the glorification of the Great in bowing.
TABATABAI:87:17-19/r8.anchor:
قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
" اجعلوها في ركوعكم "

ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.claim: Aḥwā is a circumstantial accusative modifying pasture: God brought it out green, tinged with dark hue, then dried it into brittle stubble like debris atop floodwater.
ZAJJAJ:v5p315/r5.anchor: أحوى أي أخرجه أخضر يضرب إلى الحوة، والحوة السواد.

TABRISI:87:7-9/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r6.claim: Guthāʾ is mixed vegetation and debris cast to a valley's edge by floodwater; Arabs also call mixed tribal crowds guthāʾ.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r6.anchor: والغثاء ما يقذف به السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

TABRISI:87:7-9/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r7.claim: Aḥwā means black, and ḥawa means blackness; the source adduces poetry for this usage.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r7.anchor: والأحوى الأسود والحوة السواد قال ذو الرمة

TABRISI:87:7-9/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7-9/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7-9/r12.claim: The preferred parsing makes aḥwā a circumstantial accusative describing pasture turned black by drying; it may alternatively modify guthāʾ.
TABRISI:87:7-9/r12.anchor: أحوى نصب على الحال من المرعى والتقدير أخرج المرعى أحوى أي أسود لشدة خضرته

TABRISI:87:7/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r17.claim: Aḥwā describes pasture that becomes black after turning green and drying.
TABRISI:87:7/r17.anchor: أي أسود بعد الخضرة وذلك أن الكلأ إذا يبس اسود

TABRISI:87:7/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r18.claim: Alternatively, aḥwā means intensely green, nearly black; the grass then dries after serving as fodder in both states.
TABRISI:87:7/r18.anchor: أحوى أي شديد الخضرة يضرب إلى السواد من شدة خضرته فجعله غثاء

TABRISI:87:7/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:87:7/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:87:7/r19.claim: The pasture's flourishing and disappearance is also a parable for the worldly life after its freshness fades.
TABRISI:87:7/r19.anchor: إنه مثل ضربه الله تعالى لذهاب الدنيا بعد نضارتها

ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n3/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n3/r1.claim: The herbage's decay is a metonym for God's bringing life and dealing death.
ASAD-NOTES:87:1#n3/r1.anchor: metonymically, "who brings forth life and deals death"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r2.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r2.claim: “Ghutha” is dry, broken vegetation carried by a flood and cast on a valley’s edge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r2.anchor: قال المبرد: الغثاء: ما تحطم من يبس البقل يأتي به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r3.speaker: الكلبي، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r3.claim: They gloss “ghutha” as dry, withered vegetation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r3.anchor: قال الكلبي: غثاء يبيسا (¬4). وقال مقاتل: يابسا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r4.speaker: عطاء، الكلبي، مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r4.claim: One interpretation makes “ahwa” describe the dry debris: it turns black after greenness, either as it withers or after a year.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r4.anchor: أنه من نعت الغثاء، والمعنى فجعله يابسا أسود بعد الخضرة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r5.claim: A cited poetic line supports the account that dried vegetation turns black.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة، الفراء، المبرد، الزجاج، أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r6.claim: An alternative parses “ahwa” as a circumstantial accusative describing the pasture: lush green tending toward black, then made into debris.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r6.anchor: {أحوى} في موضع نصب حال من المرعى، المعنى: الذي أخرج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r7.claim: On the second reading, “ḥawah” means blackness; a line by Dhu al-Rumma uses it for the dark hue of lips and gums.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p435/r7.anchor:
ذو الرمة:
لمياء في شفتيها حوة لعس ... وفي اللثات (¬1) وفي

WAHIDI-QT:87:5/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:87:5/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:87:5/r1.claim: The growth becomes dry debris carried by a flood, and “dark” describes it as black and decayed.
WAHIDI-QT:87:5/r1.anchor: يابسا وهو ما يحمله السيل مما يجف من النبات

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r2.claim: God turns the fresh pasture into dark flood debris, manure, or coal-like fuel; the fate of disbelievers who scheme against truth and people devoted to bodily pleasure will be worse, as fuel for the great Fire.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r2.anchor: sonra da onu kapkara bir gusâya çevirdi gübre ve kömür hâline getirdi

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r3.speaker: Âlûsî
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r3.claim: Citing al-Majmaʿ, Alusi explains ghutha as a mixed mass of scattered kinds; Arabs also call a people gathered from scattered tribes ahlat or ghutha.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r3.anchor: Arab, perakende kabilelerden toplanmış olan kavme “ahlât” ve “gusâ” tâbir ederler

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r4.claim: Ghutha is the grass, leaves, rubbish, and foam that floodwater sweeps together and throws onto banks; Elmalılı therefore renders it “sel kusuğu.”
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r4.anchor: sel suyunun mer‘alardaki otları, çöpleri birbirlerine katarak sürükleyip getirdiği

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r5.claim: Ahwa can mean black, brown, dark green, or sooty dark bay; black and brown qualify ghutha, while dark green can describe the pasture from which it becomes debris.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r5.anchor: karamsı, esmer, koyu yeşil, isli doru

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r6.claim: One reading describes green plants drying, falling, or being eaten and excreted before floods carry them away as dark combustible manure and sediment.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r6.anchor: Mer‘âlardaki yeşil nebâtâtın kuruyup dökülerek veya hayvânât tarafından yenilip

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r7.claim: A more detailed geological reading sees an allusion to combustible turf and the formation of coal deposits; both readings warn bodily-minded people of their fate, as 47:12 compares them to grazing animals.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r7.anchor: Tabakāt-ı Arz ve maden ilimlerinde bahsedildiği üzere karbon (fahm) teşekkülâtına

ELMALILI:87:4-5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r8.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r8.claim: The cited geological account describes turf as combustible material formed from decomposing plant deposits in shallow wet hollows and marshes, often with buried trees, animal remains, and layered sediment.
ELMALILI:87:4-5/r8.anchor: Akarsularda ve derin havzalarda ve suyu bazı zamanlar kuruyan mahallerde

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r1.claim: Earth scientists agree that coal deposits formed from accumulated plants, supported by microscopic remains in coal and turf and stems and leaves in adjacent clay, but they disagree on how plants accumulated.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r1.anchor: Arziyyâtçıların bu meselede re’yleri müttefiktir. Ancak terâkümün keyfiyeti hakkında müttefik değildirler

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r2.claim: One reported theory says rivers or ancient sea waves buried large volumes of plants to form coal seams.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r2.anchor: Bazıları demişlerdir ki: Rüsûbât-ı fahmiye enhâr sularının yahut mukaddemâ bazı yerlerde

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r3.claim: Another theory places most deposits in basin-like hollows on exposed land, where water carried nearby plant remains.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r3.anchor: Bazıları da demiştir ki: Bu rüsûbâtın ekserisi mekşuf arzın havzımsı hufrelerinde oluyor

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r4.claim: Elmalılı rejects the transport theory because thick seams would require implausibly deep masses of floating vegetation; the required plant layers exceed what rivers or seas could carry.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r4.anchor: Evvelki kavil merduddur. Çünkü bu surette bazı bilâdda bulunan tabakalar gibi cidden kalın kömür tabakaları

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r5.claim: He considers local accumulation in land hollows plausible because it requires only the long time needed for organic matter to accumulate.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r5.anchor: İkinci kavilde ise su‘ûbet yoktur. Bu ancak taş kömürün tekevvün ettiği uzvî maddelerin terâküm etmesi

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r6.claim: The account estimates that modern forest growth could build a thin coal layer over centuries, while ancient carbon-rich air and carbonic gas rising from Earth may have accelerated plant growth and carbon fixation.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r6.anchor: eski zamanda cev birtakım buharlarla meşhun idi, ondan cidden kuvvetli bir nebat olmuştu

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r7.claim: Coal deposits are not the only formations requiring vast time; thick fossil limestone made from shells also takes many ages.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r7.anchor: rüsûbât-ı haceriyenin tekevvünü kurûn-i adîde iktizâ eder

ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r8.claim: The turf analogy is supported by microscopic remains of aquatic plant spores in coal and turf, rooted standing trees and fossil leaves, and separate deposits across basins, all indicating marshland hollows.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#2/r8.anchor: Rüsûbât-ı fahmiyeyi turba teşbih edenlerin re’yi şununla da müeyyeddir

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r1.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r1.claim: The geological account proposes that Earth was initially flat, mountainless, and water-covered; early simple algae and sulfur-family plants were unusually large and abundant, and later burial and transformation produced coal.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r1.anchor: Arz’ı örten acîb nebatların kesretiyle muttasıftır

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r2.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r2.claim: Coal-producing plants predated animals; mountain formation buried them deeply, where later changes and slow decomposition infused the material with pitch and tar.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r2.anchor: Devr-i fahmî nebâtı zamanımızdaki nebâta bi’l-külliye muhaliftir

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r3.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r3.claim: The account attributes the enormous ancient flora to a hot, humid, foggy climate and infers similar temperatures across latitudes from fossil plants found from equatorial to polar regions.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r3.anchor: Müstemir yağmurlar, şiddetli harâret, müstemir sisle mestur hafif ziyâ

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r4.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r4.claim: The later coal period features persistent rain, extreme heat, fog, and dim light, producing flora unlike anything possible today.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r4.anchor: bunlardan husûsî bir nebat tevellüd ediyormuş ki zamanımızda ona benzerinin husûlü kābil olmuyor

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r5.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r5.claim: To picture the later coal flora, the account compares it to perpetually rainy, hot, mist-covered islands with giant fern forests, thick undergrowth, and many more fern and seed-plant species than survive today.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r5.anchor: senenin üç yüz günü yağmur düşen

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r6.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r6.claim: Fossil European coal beds contain about 250 fern species and over 120 naked-seeded plants, compared with about 50 and 25 living species respectively.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r6.anchor: Avrupa’da fahmî araziden kazılan serhasiye envâ‘ı iki yüz elli nevidir

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r7.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r7.claim: Geologists agree that coal results from slight decomposition of plants remaining in the earth; seams preserve their stems, leaves, and sometimes large tree trunks.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r7.anchor: Taş kömürü uzun müddet arzda kalan nebâtâttaki cüz’î tehallülün neticesinden ibaret

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r8.claim: Of two explanations, Elmalılı calls transport of plants from afar unlikely and local growth and decay in marshes more plausible, given the time needed for organic matter to accumulate.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r8.anchor: evvelki ihtimal ba‘îd, ikinci ihtimal akla karibdir

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r9.claim: Parallel seams and preserved fine impressions indicate that coal layers formed in complete quiet, from plants dying and decomposing where they grew in marshy places.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r9.anchor: bu tabakalar tam bir sükûnetle tekevvün etmiştir

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r10.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r10.claim: The account imagines a thin elastic crust above a fluid mass; lunar and solar tides and gradual subsidence repeatedly submerged forests, then allowed new forests to grow, accumulating plant layers over ages.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r10.anchor: Şimdiki denizlerimiz gibi Ay ve Güneş’in câzibelerine tebe‘an içindeki seyyal kütle

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r11.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r11.claim: Submerged, sponge-like plant matter slightly rotted and fermented; mineral gases were thought to enter it, while pitchy oils formed during slow decomposition.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r11.anchor: O suların bürüdüğü nebatların kütleleri hafif, isfencî idi, el’an bataklıklarda tekevvün eden turba benziyordu

ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r12.speaker: Keşfü’l-Esrâri’n-Nûrâniyyeti’l-Kur’âniyye
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r12.claim: Burial pressure and heat from Earth's interior densified coal, making lower seams drier and harder; experiments pressing heated wood in wet clay with gases trapped produced glossy or dull coal-like material.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#3/r12.anchor: Defe‘ât ile mükerrer tecribelerden fahm-ı hacerînin keyfiyyet-i tekevvünü tevazzuh etmiş

ELMALILI:87:4-5#4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:87:4-5#4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:87:4-5#4/r2.claim: A detailed view sees mineral coal as plants that died and decomposed under water; the phrase also points to this origin.
ELMALILI:87:4-5#4/r2.anchor: bütün maden kömürlerinin dahi mâhiyeti nebâtâtın sular içinde ölüp tehallül ederek çevrildiği kara bir gusâdan ibaret olduğu

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.claim: The perfects are aspectual rather than inherently past; verses 4–5 show creation as ongoing world-sustaining activity through the pasture’s recurring growth and decay.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:2-5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Dass Gottes Schöpfungstätigkeit hier nicht als einmaliger Akt, sondern als fortwährende, welterhaltende Aktivität verstanden wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r1.speaker: arabische Lexikographen
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r1.claim: Ghuṯāʾ means decayed plants and other debris floating on floodwater in a wadi.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Ġuṯāʾ (sonst noch in 23:41) meint den arabischen Lexikographen zufolge verrottete Pflanzen

CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r2.claim: Aḥwā denotes a brownish or dark green hue, though lexicons disagree on its precise shade.
CORPUSCORANICUM:87:5:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Aḥwā bezeichnet einen bräunlichen oder dunkelgrünen Farbton, dessen genaue Beschaffenheit die Lexika auf unterschiedliche Weise bestimmen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.claim: The verses may describe spring growth turning into black plant remains, or metaphorically living things receiving life and then dying.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r5.anchor: 4 ve 5. âyetler, Allah’ın baharda yeşil bitkileri bitirip vakti gelince onları kapkara bitki kalıntısı haline getirmesi şeklinde açıklandığı gibi mecazen

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r6.speaker: Bazı çağdaş yorumcular
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r6.claim: Some contemporary commentators see a reference to coal formation: ancient vegetation became coal under underground heat and pressure, another sign of divine power.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:87:1/r6.anchor: Bazı çağdaş yorumcular 5. âyetin, kömür madeninin teşekkülüne işaret ettiğini ileri sürmüşlerdir

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367/r1.claim: Qatāda says ghuthāʾ is decayed matter and aḥwā describes growth that passes through yellow, green, and white before drying.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p367/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ غثاء ﴾ قال الغثاء الشيء البالي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is plant matter washed onto a valley's edge; the root can mean a mixture of diverse species, and the plural aghthāʾ is unusual.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r1.anchor: غثاء هو ما يقذف به السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r2.claim: Here ghuthāʾ is dried vegetation; aḥwā means black or brown, though intense green is also explained as appearing black at first glance, supported by a line of Dhu al-Rumma.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r2.anchor: والمراد به هنا اليابس من النبات أي فجعله بعد ذلك يابسا أحوى من الحوة وهي كما قيل السواد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r3.claim: Aḥwā may instead describe the fresh pasture as intensely green before it becomes debris; Alusi calls this reading less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r3.anchor: وجوز كونه حالا من المرعى أي أخرج المرعى حال كونه طريا غضا شديد الخضرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r4.claim: The rapid sequence from freshness to dry debris emphasizes the abrupt change; the successive descriptions also express gradual growth and divine nurturing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p104#3/r4.anchor: وسر التقديم المبالغة في استعقاب حالة الجفاف حالة الرفيف والغضارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r2.claim: After it is green, God makes the pasture dry, decayed, and black, like foam floating on a torrent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p400#2/r2.anchor: هشيما باليا، كالغثاء الذي تراه فوق السيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r6.claim: The pasture's drying and darkening after greenness displays God's complete power and choice through the alternation of opposites in the same substance; غثاء is its scattered, dried debris and أحوى its darkening color.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p395#2/r6.anchor: ولما كان إيباسه وتسويده بعد اخضراره ونموه في غاية الدلالة على تمام القدرة وكمال الاختيار بمعاقبة الأضداد

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ, with light or doubled thāʾ, is grass, plants, and scraps cast by a flood onto a valley's edge; an unnamed poet uses it for torrent debris.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r1.anchor: ما يقذف به السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reports al-ighthāʾ as a plural; Abū Ḥayyān calls it unusual because it forms afʿāl from fiʿāl.

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r3.claim: Al-ḥuwwa is a black tint tending toward green; Dhū al-Rummah's poem uses it for a woman's lips and gums.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r3.anchor: قال ذو الرّمة : لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r4.claim: A second gloss is green with black; another poetic usage describes aḥwāʾ as a gazelle with two black and white stripes on its back.

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r5.claim: The gazelle sense is specified as having two black and white stripes along its back, with a poem cited as evidence.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r5.anchor: والأحوى : الظبي الذي في ظهره خطان من سواد وبياض

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r6.speaker: الجوهري
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r6.anchor: وفي الصحاح : الحوة : سمرة ،   وقال الأعلم

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r7.speaker: الأعلم
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r7.claim: Al-Aʿlam first describes the color as tending toward black.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r7.anchor: وقال الأعلم : لون يضرب إلى السواد

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r8.speaker: الأعلم
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r8.claim: Al-Aʿlam also describes it as intense green tending toward black.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r8.anchor: وقال أيضاً : الشديد الخضرة التي تضرب إلى السواد

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r9.claim: The apparent syntax makes aḥwāʾ an adjective qualifying ghuthāʾ.

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says old flood debris turns black and rots when rain reaches it.
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس : المعنى { فجعله غثاء أحوى } : أي أسود

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r11.claim: Alternatively, aḥwāʾ is a circumstantial accusative of al-marʿā, intensely green and tending to black through plentiful water.

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r12.claim: The adjective is delayed to suit the verse endings.

ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:87:5/r13.claim: A further poem describes rain and its luxuriant growth.

ALUSI:87:5/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is vegetation and grass cast by a flood onto a valley bank; it originally denotes mixtures of different kinds.
ALUSI:87:5/r1.anchor: هو ما يقذف به السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

ALUSI:87:5/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r2.speaker: المجمع
ALUSI:87:5/r2.claim: Al-Majmaʿ explains the term as a mixture of diverse kinds; Arabs also call people gathered from different tribes mixed groups or ghuthāʾ.
ALUSI:87:5/r2.anchor: وأصله على ما في المجمع الاخلاط من أجناس شتى والعرب تسمى القوم

ALUSI:87:5/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r3.claim: The word is also pronounced with doubled thāʾ; its plural aghthāʾ is unusual because it forms afʿāl from fiʿāl.
ALUSI:87:5/r3.anchor: ويقال غثاء بالتشديد وجاء جمعه على أغثاء وهو غريب من حيث جمع فعال

ALUSI:87:5/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r4.claim: Here ghuthāʾ means dried vegetation: God turns the pasture into dry plant matter.
ALUSI:87:5/r4.anchor: والمراد به هنا اليابس من النبات أي فجعله بعد ذلك يابساً

ALUSI:87:5/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r5.claim: Al-Ḥawah is said to mean black; al-Aʿlam describes a shade tending toward black, while al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines it as brown, so aḥwā means black or brown.
ALUSI:87:5/r5.anchor: من الحوة وهي كما قيل السواد وقال الأعلم لون يضرب إلى السواد وفي الصحاح الحوة السمرة

ALUSI:87:5/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r6.claim: Dry vegetation turns black or brown, making aḥwā an emphatic adjective describing the ghuthāʾ.
ALUSI:87:5/r6.anchor: والنبات إذا يبس أسود أو اسمر فهو صفة مؤكدة للغثاء

ALUSI:87:5/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r7.claim: Al-ḥawah can also mean intense greenness; Dhu al-Rummah cites it of lips and gums, which does not conflict with blackness because intense green initially looks black.
ALUSI:87:5/r7.anchor: وتفسر الحوة بشدة الخضرة وعليه قول ذي الرمة

ALUSI:87:5/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r8.claim: Aḥwā could instead be a circumstantial accusative of al-marʿā: the pasture is first fresh and intensely green, then becomes debris.
ALUSI:87:5/r8.anchor: وجوز كونه حالاً من المرعى أي أخرج المرعى حال كونه طريا غضا شديد الخضرة

ALUSI:87:5/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r9.claim: On that alternative parsing, an intervening coordinated phrase does not invalidate the link between the circumstantial accusative and its referent, especially since the states follow without delay.
ALUSI:87:5/r9.anchor: والفصل بالمعطوف بين الحال وصاحبها ليس فصلا بأجنبي لاسيما وهو حال

ALUSI:87:5/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r10.claim: Putting the green state first intensifies its quick succession by dryness, as though the pasture became debris before its greenness fully developed; this reading is contrary to the apparent construction.
ALUSI:87:5/r10.anchor: وسر التقديم المبالغة في استعقاب حالة الجفاف حالة الرفيف والغضارة

ALUSI:87:5/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:87:5/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:87:5/r11.claim: The successive descriptions imply gradual development, conveying nurturing as bringing something to completion little by little.
ALUSI:87:5/r11.anchor: وهذه الأوصاف على ما قيل يتضمن كل منها التدريج ففي الوصف بها تحقيق لمعنى التربية

BAGHAWI:87:5/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:5/r1.claim: After it is green, the pasture becomes withered, decayed debris like the material seen atop a torrent.
BAGHAWI:87:5/r1.anchor: { فجعله } بعد الخضرة ،   { غثاءً } هشيماً بالياً ،   كالغثاء الذي تراه فوق السيل .

BAGHAWI:87:5/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:87:5/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:87:5/r2.claim: Aḥwā means black after greenness; dried, withered herbage turns black.
BAGHAWI:87:5/r2.anchor: { أحوى } أسود بعد الخضرة ، وذلك أن الكلأ إذا جف ويبس اسود

BAYDAWI:87:5/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:5/r1.claim: One explanation is that after becoming green the pasture turns into dry, black refuse.
BAYDAWI:87:5/r1.anchor: فجعله بعد خضرته غثاء أحوى يابسا أسود

BAYDAWI:87:5/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:87:5/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:87:5/r2.claim: Alternatively, aḥwā is a circumstantial description of the pasture: God brought it forth black from the intensity of its greenness.
BAYDAWI:87:5/r2.anchor: وقيل أحوى حال من المرعى أي أخرجه أحوى أي أسود من شدة خضرته

BIQAI:87:5/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r1.claim: The drying and darkening of grown greenery shows God's complete power and choice, bringing opposites together in one substance.
BIQAI:87:5/r1.anchor: ولما كان إيباسه وتسويده بعد اخضراره

BIQAI:87:5/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r2.claim: Ghuthāʾ means abundant plant matter, which dries, breaks apart, and is gathered by floodwater into froth, ruin, and fragments on the ground.
BIQAI:87:5/r2.anchor: أي بعد أطوار من زمن إخراجه

BIQAI:87:5/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r3.claim: Aḥwā may describe vegetation saturated to blackish green, red tending to black, or green so intense that it tends toward black.
BIQAI:87:5/r3.anchor: حتى صار أسود يضرب إلى خضرة

BIQAI:87:5/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r4.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI:87:5/r4.claim: Al-Qazzāz defines ḥuwa as a horse-coat shade between black and chestnut; Biqāʿī says usage broadened until aḥwā could mean any black thing.
BIQAI:87:5/r4.anchor: وقال القزاز رحمه الله في ديوانه : الحوة شية من شيات الخيل ، وهى بين الدهمة والكمتة ، وكثر هذا حتى سموا كل أسود أحوى

BIQAI:87:5/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r5.claim: He also allows that the plant becomes black from severe drying, then winds gather its fragments from every direction.
BIQAI:87:5/r5.anchor: أنه أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح

BIQAI:87:5/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r6.claim: Both terms carry senses of life and death; aḥwā comes second because its stronger association with green growth would otherwise constrain its sense.
BIQAI:87:5/r6.anchor: فيجوز أن يريد حينئذ أنه أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح وجمعته من كل أوب حيت تفتت ، فكل من الكلمتين فيها حياة وموت ، وأخر الثانية لتحملهما

BIQAI:87:5/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r7.claim: Natural dispositions have only fixed, necessary effects: fire burns what it touches and cannot then transform it into another quality; divine action can unite opposites.

BIQAI:87:5/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:87:5/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI:87:5/r8.claim: The pasture's yearly beginning and end recall resurrection; it is especially apt because cultivated growth crumbles to soil and God restores it with water just as He will restore the dead.
BIQAI:87:5/r8.anchor: وأشار بالبداية والنهاية إلى تذكر ذلك ، وأنه على سبيل التكرار في كل عام الدال على بعث الخلائق ، وخص المرعى لأنه أدل على البعث

DURR:87:5/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:87:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ghuthāʾ as debris or withered fragments and aḥwā as changed in color.
DURR:87:5/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فجعله غثاء } قال : هشيماً { أحوى } قال : متغيراً .

DURR:87:5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:5/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR:87:5/r2.claim: Qatada calls ghuthāʾ a worn-out thing and describes the plant changing through yellow, green, and white before drying after its greenness.
DURR:87:5/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { فجعله غثاء أحوى } قال : الغثاء الشيء البالي

DURR:87:5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:87:5/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:87:5/r3.claim: Mujahid identifies the ghuthāʾ as flood debris and aḥwā as black.
DURR:87:5/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد { فجعله غثاء أحوى } قال : غثاء السيل

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried, withered, broken vegetation carried by floodwaters; people of no worth are likened to it.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r1.anchor: ما يبس وجف وتحطم من النبات ، وهو الذي يحمله السيل ، وبه يشبه الناس الذين لا قدر لهم

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r2.claim: One explanation takes aḥwā as green with a black cast caused by intense greenness and freshness.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r2.anchor: قيل هو الأخضر الذي عليه سواد من شدة الخضرة والغضارة

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r3.claim: Another explanation takes aḥwā as black, tending toward green.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r3.anchor: وقيل هو الأسود سواداً يضرب إلى الخضرة

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r4.speaker: ذي الرمة
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r4.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's description of a woman's lips uses ḥuwwa for blackness tending green, illustrating the color sense.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r4.anchor: ومنه قول ذي الرمة : [ البسيط ] لمياء في شفتيها حوّة لعس . . . وفي اللثاث وفي أنيابها شنب

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r5.claim: Qatāda reads the plant as first aḥwā, dark from greenness and freshness, then ghuthāʾ once it dries.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r5.anchor: قال قتادة : تقدير هذه الآية { أخرج المرعى } ، { أحوى } أسود من خضرته ونضارته ، { فجعله غثاء } عند يبسه

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r6.claim: In Qatāda's parsing, aḥwā is a circumstantial accusative describing the pasture when brought forth.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r6.anchor: قال قتادة : تقدير هذه الآية { أخرج المرعى } ، { أحوى } أسود من خضرته ونضارته ، { فجعله غثاء } عند يبسه ، ف { أحوى } حال

IBNATIYYA:87:5/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says old flood debris turns black and rots after rain, becoming aḥwā in that state.
IBNATIYYA:87:5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : المعنى { فجعله غثاء أحوى } أي أسود ، لأن الغثاء إذا قدم وأصابته الأمطار اسود وتعفن فصار { أحوى } بهذه الصفة

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains it as dry vegetation that has changed color.

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r2.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r2.claim: Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd are reported to give the same explanation as Ibn Abbas: withered, changed vegetation.
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r2.anchor: وعن مجاهد ، وقتادة ، وابن زيد ، نحوه

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.claim: Some Arab-language scholars take the word order as postponed: God brought forth dark-green pasture, then made it debris.
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r3.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب{[29970]}  يرى أن ذلك من المؤخر الذي معناه التقديم

IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir rejects the possible inverted order because it conflicts with the exegetes’ transmitted explanations.
IBNKATHIR:87:5/r4.anchor: ثم قال ابن جرير : وهذا وإن كان محتملا إلا أنه غير صواب ؛ لمخالفته أقوال أهل التأويل

MAWARDI:87:5/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:5/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI:87:5/r1.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is vegetation dried into brittle fragments scattered by wind, and al-aḥwā means black; Dhū al-Rumma’s verse illustrates the latter.
MAWARDI:87:5/r1.anchor: وفي اللثات وفي أنيابها شنب وهذا معنى قول مجاهد

MAWARDI:87:5/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:5/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI:87:5/r2.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is vegetation carried off by a flood, and al-aḥwā means changed in color.
MAWARDI:87:5/r2.anchor: والأحوى : المتغير ، وهذا معنى قول السدي

MAWARDI:87:5/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:5/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:87:5/r3.claim: A reversed order means the plant first becomes dark with living colors—green, red, yellow, and white—then turns to dry debris; the colors are collectively called black, as in al-Sawād of Iraq, with a verse by Imruʾ al-Qays as evidence.
MAWARDI:87:5/r3.anchor: الثالث : أن في الكلام تقديما وتأخيرا ، ومعناه أحوى

MAWARDI:87:5/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:87:5/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:87:5/r4.claim: God compares disbelievers to dead, dry growth to show worldly life disappearing after its freshness.
MAWARDI:87:5/r4.anchor: قال قتادة : وهو مثل ضربه الله تعالى للكفار لذهاب الدنيا بعد نضارتها

NASAFI:87:5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:87:5/r1.claim: The pasture becomes dry, brittle stubble, and “aḥwā” means black; it describes the stubble.
NASAFI:87:5/r1.anchor: { فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَاءً } يابساً هشيماً { أحوى } أسود

QURTUBI:87:5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is vegetation, grass, and debris cast by floods onto valley sides; the form may also be intensified, and its plural is aghthāʾ.
QURTUBI:87:5/r1.anchor: الغثاء : ما يقذف به السيل على جوانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات والقماش

QURTUBI:87:5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:87:5/r2.claim: Qatāda glosses ghuthāʾ as something dry; crushed, dried greens and useless debris around water are also called ghuthāʾ or hasheem.
QURTUBI:87:5/r2.anchor: قتادة : الغثاء : الشيء اليابس .   ويقال للبقل والحشيش إذا تحطم ويبس

QURTUBI:87:5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r3.claim: The term also describes water covered by useless foam and floating debris.
QURTUBI:87:5/r3.anchor: وكذلك الماء : إذا علاه من الزبد والقماش ما لا ينتفع به

QURTUBI:87:5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r4.claim: Aḥwā means black; vegetation can darken almost to black through intense greenness, since ḥawa means blackness.
QURTUBI:87:5/r4.anchor: والأحوى : الأسود ، أي أن النبات يضرب إلى الحوة من شدة الخضرة كالأسود

QURTUBI:87:5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r5.speaker: الأعشى
QURTUBI:87:5/r5.claim: The cited poem uses ḥawa for a slight dark-brown tint of the lips, a desirable shade.

QURTUBI:87:5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r6.speaker: الصحاح
QURTUBI:87:5/r6.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines ḥawa as the brownness of a lip; aḥwā describes a man, ḥawwā a woman, and a camel may be green mixed with black.

QURTUBI:87:5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r7.claim: Aḥwā may be a circumstantial qualifier of al-marʿā, with the sense that God brought it out dark-green before making it debris.
QURTUBI:87:5/r7.anchor: يجوز أن يكون " أحوى " حالا من " المرعى " ، ويكون المعنى : كأنه من خضرته

QURTUBI:87:5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r8.claim: Alternatively, ḥawā is an adjective of ghuthāʾ: the vegetation became debris after being green.
QURTUBI:87:5/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون " حوى " صفة ل " غثاء " . والمعنى : أنه صار كذلك بعد خضرته

QURTUBI:87:5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:87:5/r9.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the plant becomes black from burning and age; fresh vegetation turns black when dry.
QURTUBI:87:5/r9.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة : فجعله أسود من احتراقه وقدمه ، والرطب إذا يبس أسود

QURTUBI:87:5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r10.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI:87:5/r10.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says God first brought out green pasture, then it dried, blackened, and became debris carried off by wind and floods.
QURTUBI:87:5/r10.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد : أخرج المرعى أخضر ، ثم لما يبس أسود من احتراقه

QURTUBI:87:5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI:87:5/r11.claim: The plant's loss of freshness is an image of unbelievers and the world's disappearance after its bloom.
QURTUBI:87:5/r11.anchor: وهو مثل ضربه الله تعالى للكفار ، لذهاب الدنيا بعد نضارتها

QURTUBI:87:5/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:87:5/r12.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI:87:5/r12.claim: Al-Kisāʾī cites ḥawiya al-nabāt and a line about dark, rain-grown valleys as evidence for the verb describing vegetation turning dark.

RAZI:87:5/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried vegetation carried off by wadis and water and blown about by winds.
RAZI:87:5/r1.anchor: الغثاء ما يبس من النبت فحملته الأودية والمياه وألوت به الرياح

RAZI:87:5/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r2.speaker: قطرب
RAZI:87:5/r2.claim: Quṭrub gives ghuthāʾah as the singular form of ghuthāʾ.

RAZI:87:5/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r3.anchor: الحوة السواد ، وقال بعضهم : الأحوى هو الذي يضرب إلى السواد

RAZI:87:5/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r4.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI:87:5/r4.claim: Some say aḥwā describes something that tends toward black when touched by moisture.
RAZI:87:5/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الأحوى هو الذي يضرب إلى السواد إذا أصابته رطوبة

RAZI:87:5/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r5.claim: On the first analysis, aḥwā describes the residue: pasture dries after being green and changes to black.
RAZI:87:5/r5.anchor: أنه نعت الغثاء أي صار بعد الخضرة يابسا فتغير إلى السواد

RAZI:87:5/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r6.claim: One cause of the blackening is cold drying the grass; cold whitens wet things and blackens dry ones.
RAZI:87:5/r6.anchor: ومن شأن البرودة أنها تبيض الرطب وتسود اليابس

RAZI:87:5/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r7.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r7.claim: Floodwater can make the residue black by sticking muddy particles to it.
RAZI:87:5/r7.anchor: أن يحملها السيل فيلصق بها أجزاء كدرة فتسود

RAZI:87:5/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r8.claim: Wind can make the residue black by attaching abundant dust to it.
RAZI:87:5/r8.anchor: أن يحملها الريح فتلصق بها الغبار الكثير فتسود

RAZI:87:5/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r9.speaker: الفراء وأبو عبيدة
RAZI:87:5/r9.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and Abū ʿUbaydah take aḥwā as black from the intensity of its greenness, like mudhāmmatān.
RAZI:87:5/r9.anchor: اختيار الفراء وأبي عبيدة ، وهو أن يكون الأحوى هو الأسود

RAZI:87:5/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:87:5/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:87:5/r10.claim: The alternative syntax makes the pasture first aḥwā and then ghuthāʾ, as in saying the Book was made upright and not crooked.
RAZI:87:5/r10.anchor: والتقدير الذي أخرج المرعى أحوى فجعله غثاء

TAB:87:5/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r1.speaker: author
TAB:87:5/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried, withered vegetation that the wind carries away.

TAB:87:5/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r2.speaker: author
TAB:87:5/r2.claim: Aḥwā describes the plant turning black after being white or green because of severe drying.

TAB:87:5/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:87:5/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as withered debris that has changed color.
TAB:87:5/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   في قوله :  غُثاءً أحْوَى

TAB:87:5/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:87:5/r4.claim: Mujahid compares it to flood debris and explains aḥwā as black.

TAB:87:5/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB:87:5/r5.claim: Qatada says the growth returns to dryness after being green.

TAB:87:5/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:87:5/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says green plants wither into dark debris carried off by winds and floods.
TAB:87:5/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد ،   في قوله :  فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوَى

TAB:87:5/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r7.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB:87:5/r7.claim: Some Arabists propose fronting and postponement: the pasture is first aḥwā, dark green, then becomes ghuthāʾ.
TAB:87:5/r7.anchor: وكان بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب يرى أن ذلك من المؤخّر الذي معناه التقديم

TAB:87:5/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r8.speaker: author
TAB:87:5/r8.claim: The cited line by Dhu al-Rumma supports Arab usage of black for vegetation whose green color is especially intense.
TAB:87:5/r8.anchor: أن يكون ما اشتدّت خضرته من النبات

TAB:87:5/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:87:5/r9.speaker: author
TAB:87:5/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the inversion because the wording has a sound meaning in its present order; inversion is needed only when no direct sense works.
TAB:87:5/r9.anchor: غير صواب عندي بخلافه تأويل أهل التأويل في أن الحرف إنما يحتال لمعناه المخرج بالتقديم والتأخير

BURHAN:v4p297/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p297/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p297/r3.claim: Fa can also be a coordinating conjunction alone, as in the sequence making the vegetation dry and dark.
BURHAN:v4p297/r3.anchor: وعكسه عكسها بمجرد العطف فيما سبق من نحو

BURHAN:v3p279/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r7.claim: The phrase means dark-green chaff; placing aḥwā after ghuthāʾ serves the rhyme.
BURHAN:v3p279/r7.anchor: إلى السواد والموجب لتأخير ﴿ أحوى ﴾ رعاية الفواصل

BURHAN:v1p303/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p303/r2.speaker: أحد القولين
BURHAN:v1p303/r2.claim: One interpretation takes ‘aḥwā’ as blackened by drying and withering.
BURHAN:v1p303/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه الأسود من الجفاف واليبس

BURHAN:v1p303/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p303/r3.speaker: الثاني
BURHAN:v1p303/r3.claim: The opposing interpretation takes ‘aḥwā’ as black from intense greenness, as in ‘both dark green gardens.’
BURHAN:v1p303/r3.anchor: والثانى أنه الأسود من شدة الخضرة

BURHAN:v1p303/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p303/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p303/r4.claim: On the dryness reading it modifies the refuse; on the greenness reading it is circumstantial of the pasture, and is delayed to suit the verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p303/r4.anchor: فعلى الأول هو صفة لغثاء وعلى الثاني هو حال من المرعى وأخر لتناسب الفواصل

ITQAN:v2p528/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p528/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p528/r10.claim: If ghuthāʾan aḥwā means blackened by dryness, aḥwā describes the debris; if it means intensely green, it is circumstantial of the pasture.
ITQAN:v2p528/r10.anchor: وقوله ﴿ غثاء أحوى ﴾ إن أريد به الأسود من الجفاف واليبس فهو صفة لغثاء أو من شدة الخضرة فحال من المرعى

ITQAN:v3p269/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p269/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p269/r7.claim: The adjective may be separated from its noun; ahwa can be read as describing al-marʿa across the intervening clause.
ITQAN:v3p269/r7.anchor: الثالث والثلاثون الفصل بين الموصوف والصفة نحو

ITQAN:v3p34/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p34/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p34/r2.claim: If “dark” means green, it describes the pasture; the order is changed for the verse ending.
ITQAN:v3p34/r2.anchor: على تفسير ( أحوى ) بالأخضر وجعله نعتا للمرعى

QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p414/r14.claim: The vegetation becomes withered flood-scum and black.

FARRA:v3p256/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r6.claim: Dried vegetation is ghuthaʾ; ahwa describes vegetation darkened by age.
FARRA:v3p256/r6.anchor: إذا صار النبت يبيسا فهو غثاء

FARRA:v3p256/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p256/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p256/r7.claim: Alternatively, syntax is reordered: God brought forth dark pasture and then made it withered debris.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.claim: The preceding sūrah urges the Prophet to wait: persistent deniers receive only temporary respite under God's practice, and cannot escape His grasp.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r1.anchor: Sūrah al-Ṭāriq, the previous sūrah ended on urging the Prophet (sws) to show patience and to wait for the decision of God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.claim: This sūrah shifts its primary address from stubborn Quraysh to the Prophet and, over at least ten following sūrahs, dispels his preaching fears in varied ways.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r2.anchor: while ignoring these stubborn elements from among the Quraysh, the Prophet (sws) is addressed directly and given glad tidings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p270/r3.claim: Verses 1–5 direct the Prophet to glorify God, whose attributes show that creation and human physical and intellectual capacities mature gradually.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.claim: He rejects the common decay-based readings of black litter or waste: aḥwā describes reddish or greenish blackness produced by freshness, fertility, and luxuriant growth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r1.anchor: because of freshness, fertility and luxuriance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r2.speaker: Ta’bbata Sharraṇ
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r2.claim: The cited jāhili poet uses the description while praising a robust, healthy young man, supporting this fresh, vigorous sense of aḥwā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r2.anchor: the famous poet of the jāhilliyah period, Ta’bbata Sharra ṇ, while extolling a person says

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.claim: Through Imām al-Farāhī, the author cites Qaṭṭāmī's valley couplet depicting dense, layered undergrowth as evidence that ghuthāʾ can mean fertile luxuriant vegetation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p275/r3.anchor: he wrote while praising a valley

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.claim: Because aḥwā does not denote decay-blackness and qualifies ghuthāʾ, the phrase means God brings out vegetation and makes it luxuriant and blackish green.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p276/r1.anchor: makes them luxuriant and blackish green

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r2.claim: Ḥawāʾ is blackness tinged with green; Dhū al-Rumma's line uses it of a woman's lip.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r2.anchor: الحوة: سواد يضرب إلى الخضرة، قال ذو الرمة:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r3.claim: Another view makes ḥawāʾ green overlaid with black; al-aḥwāʾ may also be a gazelle with black and white back stripes, illustrated by an unnamed poet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r3.anchor: وقيل: خضرة عليها سواد، والأحوى: الظبي الذي في ظهره خطان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r4.speaker: الأعلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r4.claim: Al-Aʿlam describes ḥawāʾ as a color tending toward black, including intense green tending toward black.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r4.anchor: وقال الأعلم: لون يضرب إلى السواد، وقال أيضا: الشديد الخضرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r5.speaker: الصحاح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p454/r5.anchor: وفي الصحاح: الحوة: سمرة، وقال الأعلم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r15.claim: The apparent syntax makes aḥwā an adjective of ghuthāʾ; Ibn ʿAbbās explains blackness as old flood debris that rots after rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r15.anchor: والظاهر أن أحوى صفة لغثاء. قال ابن عباس: المعنى فجعله غثاء أحوى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r16.claim: Another reading makes aḥwā a circumstantial description of pasture, dark from intense, well-watered greenness; its delay preserves the verse endings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p455/r16.anchor: وقيل: أحوى حال من المرعى، أي أحرى المرعى أحوى، أي للسواد من شدة خضرته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r1.claim: A cited verse describes rainfall and greenness, continuing the discussion of pasture's dark green color.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p456/r1.anchor: وغيث من الوسمي حوتلاعه ... تبطنته بشيظم صلتان

BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r2.claim: After becoming green, the pasture is made dry and black; alternatively, aḥwā describes pasture made black by intense greenness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:87:4-7/r2.anchor: بعد خضرته. { غثاء أحوى } يابسا أسود.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r1.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r1.claim: Al-Qazzaz defines ḥawa as a horse coat between deep black and dark bay; usage broadened it to mean any black thing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r1.anchor: وقال القزاز رحمه الله في ديوانه : الحوة شية من شيات الخيل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r2.claim: The vegetation may be dark from extreme dryness, swept together by winds and crumbled; the wording combines signs of life and death.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r2.anchor: أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح وجمعته من كل أوب حيت تفتت

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r3.claim: Placing the second descriptor last permits it to carry both its stronger green meaning and the contrasting black meaning.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r3.anchor: وأخر الثانية لتحملها لأن دلالتها على الخضرة أتم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r4.claim: The combination of opposites points to one freely acting God; created natural powers have only fixed, necessary effects, like fire that can only burn.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r4.anchor: فدل جمعه بين الأضداد على الذات الواحدة على كمال الاختيار

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r5.claim: The plant's recurring beginning and end remind people of resurrection: vegetation becomes dust, then God restores it with water as He restores the dead.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r5.anchor: ثم يعيده سبحانه بالماء على ما كان عليه سواء كما يفعل بالأموات سواء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r6.claim: Pasture is singled out as evidence for resurrection because people cultivate it, and its decay and renewal parallel the dead's restoration.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p396/r6.anchor: وخص المرعى لأنه أدل على البعث لأنه مما ينبته الناس

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses ghutha as dried fragments and ahwa as changed in color.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {فجعله غثاء} قال: هشيما {أحوى} قال: متغيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r9.claim: Qatada says ghutha is decayed matter; ahwa is yellow, green, and white before drying after its green stage.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {فجعله غثاء أحوى} قال: الغثاء الشيء البالي

DURR-FULL:v8p482/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies ghutha as flood debris and ahwa as black.
DURR-FULL:v8p482/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد {فجعله غثاء أحوى} قال: غثاء السيل و {أحوى} قال: أسود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r1.claim: The plant's swift change from growth to chaff embeds a reminder of death after life, as in the human progression from weakness to strength and back.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r1.anchor: إدماج العبرة بتصاريف ما أودع الله في المخلوقات من مختلف الأطوار من الشيء إلى ضده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r2.claim: The transition particle suggests the brief span between verdant growth and chaff, like worldly vegetation that quickly becomes a vanished harvest.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p279/r2.anchor: الحرف الموضوع لعطف ما يحصل فيه حكم المعطوف بعد زمن قريب من زمن حصول المعطوف عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r11.claim: Ghutha is dried, brittle vegetation carried by floodwater and can describe people of little worth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r11.anchor: ما يبس وجف وتحطم من النبات، وهو الذي يحمله السيل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r12.claim: Ahwa may mean dark green from lushness or black tinged with green, as in Dhu al-Rumma's description of dark lips.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r12.anchor: قيل هو الأخضر الذي عليه سواد من شدة الخضرة والغضارة، وقيل هو الأسود سوادا يضرب إلى الخضرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r13.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r13.claim: Qatada construes the syntax as God bringing out luxuriantly dark-green pasture, then making it chaff when it dries; ahwa is circumstantial.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r13.anchor: قال قتادة: تقدير هذه الآية أخرج المرعى، أحوى أسود من خضرته ونضارته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas says the old chaff becomes black and rotten after rain, explaining ghutha ahwa as black.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p468#3/r14.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى فجعله غثاء أحوى أي أسود، لأن الغثاء إذا قدم وأصابته الأمطار

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r9.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is plant debris carried by a flood and left beside a valley; it also denotes mixed scraps or a mixed crowd.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r9.anchor: والغثاء: ما تقدم به السيل على جانب الوادي من النبات. والحشيش، وأصله الأخلاط من أصناف شتى

JISHUMI:v10p7372/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r10.claim: Al-aḥwā means black; al-ḥawah denotes blackness, as shown by Dhu al-Rummah’s description of dark lips.
JISHUMI:v10p7372/r10.anchor: والأحوى: الأسود، والحوة: السواد، قال ذو الرمة: لمياء في شفتيها حوة لعس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r1.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is dead, dried vegetation; Qatadah says it pictures the world’s disappearance after the unbelievers’ prosperity fades.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p253/r1.anchor: والغثاء : الميت اليابس , قال قتادة : وهو مثل ضربه الله تعالى للكفار لذهاب الدنيا بعد نضارتها .

MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.claim: God brings out winter herbage and pasture, then turns its fresh green growth dry and dark.
MUQATIL:87:1-7/r5.anchor: الذي أخرج الحشيش والكلأ في الشتاء، فتراه رطبا فيجعله بعد الرطوبة، والخضرة إلى اليبوسة

TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.claim: Creation and fashioning here cover composed creatures; the first four verses describe divine governance and prove absolute lordship.
TABATABAI:87:1-19/r10.anchor: والخلق والتسوية وإن كانا مطلقين لكنهما إنما يشملان ما فيه تركيب

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r3.claim: Ghuthāʾ is flood-carried vegetation deposited beside a valley, here dried plants; aḥwā means black.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r3.anchor: الغثاء ما يقذفه السيل على جانب الوادي من الحشيش والنبات

TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.claim: Pasture growth and its change into dark dry refuse exemplify divine governance.
TABATABAI:87:1-19#2/r4.anchor: وإخراج المرعى لتغذي الحيوان ثم جعله غثاء أحوى من مصاديق التدبير الربوبي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r5.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dried plant matter carried by a flood; aḥwā is black and withered.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:87:1-6/r5.anchor: { فجعله غثاء } يابسا وهو ما يحمله السيل مما يجف من النبات
